move.title: Toast, ladle, stir
move.body: Risotto is rice cooked by adding hot broth a ladle at a time and stirring, so the grains rub against each other and release starch into a creamy sauce while keeping a firm center. You'll brown the mushrooms hard first, toast the arborio, ladle and stir for 18 minutes, then finish it off the heat with butter and parmesan (the mantecatura).

why.title: Brown the mushrooms first
why.body: Mushrooms are mostly water. In a crowded pan they steam gray. In a hot, roomy pan in batches they brown and taste meaty.

why.title: Toast the rice
why.body: Arborio stirred in fat for 2 minutes turns translucent at the edges; its outer layer sets slightly, so the grains release starch gradually instead of turning to mush.

why.title: Hot broth, a ladle at a time
why.body: Cold broth stalls the cooking. Each ladle of hot broth is stirred until nearly absorbed; the stirring scrubs starch from the grain surface.

why.title: Off the heat, butter and cheese
why.body: Beating in cold butter and parmesan off the heat emulsifies the starch, fat, and liquid into a loose, glossy sauce. It should flow slowly on a plate.

wrong.fix: It cooked too long or sat. Loosen it with a ladle of hot broth right before serving.
Keep adding broth and stirring 3 to 5 minutes more.

wrong.sign: The mushrooms are gray and wet
wrong.fix: The pan was crowded. Brown them in two batches next time.

quiz.q: Why is the broth kept hot?
quiz.explain: It goes in a ladle at a time.

choices: Scrubs starch off the grains into a creamy sauce

quiz.q: When do the butter and cheese go in?
choices: Off the heat at the end

steps.text: Heat the broth in the saucepan and keep it at a bare simmer.
Slice the mushrooms ¼ inch thick. Dice the onion fine and mince the garlic.
Brown the mushrooms in 2 tablespoons of oil in the skillet over medium-high heat in two batches, without stirring for the first 2 minutes. Season with salt and thyme and set aside.
steps.look: Deep golden on the cut sides.

steps.text: Sweat the onion in the last tablespoon of oil in the large pot over medium heat until translucent, then add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the rice and stir until the edges are translucent and it smells toasty.
Add the juice of half the lemon and stir until absorbed.
Add a ladle of hot broth and stir until nearly absorbed. Keep adding broth a ladle at a time, stirring often, at a lively simmer.
steps.tip: Taste at 15 minutes: you want a small firm center, not chalk.

target.look: Tender with a small firm center; the rice flows slowly when the pot is tilted

steps.text: Fold in the mushrooms with a last half ladle of broth. Off the heat, stir in the cold butter and parmesan hard with the wooden spoon. Season with pepper and the rest of the lemon to taste.
steps.look: Glossy and loose: it spreads slowly on a plate.
